label: D2 after a rare a2->S1 transition, mostly when the previous trial was rewarded
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the agent chose a2 and landed in S1 (a rare transition): (D2 & a2 & S1) covers 99.99% of activations and mass (dev precision 0.60). Inside that set it is gated by the previous trial being rewarded (the D1 reward input of this trial): adding prev_reward==1 gives dev P 0.79 / R 0.84 / F1 0.82 / mass recall 0.91, and it covers all of the top two activation quartiles. The misses are weak activations on a2->S1 D2 steps after an unrewarded trial. Magnitude also follows the agent being confident in a2 (choice logit < -4.4 holds for 99% of mass; with that condition instead, F1 is 0.81), and the value output in its middle range (7.1-7.5). It never fires at D1 or GO, after a1, or in S2 (so never on common a2->S2). Uses only observed inputs: the current action/state and the previous reward.

issues: None of the factual claims failed. On test: the unit never fires off D2 (F1 0). It never fires in S2 (0 activations). D2 & in_action==1 catches only about 5 of 33608 activations. D2 & a2 & S1 covers 99.99% of activations and of activation mass with precision 0.588, matching the reported 0.60 on dev.

The recorded predicate's test scores reproduce: P 0.783, R 0.836, F1 0.809, mass recall 0.902. Top two activation quartiles are covered at 0.993 and 0.999. Misses are 9.8% of mass and mostly weak activations (rel 0.1-0.5) on a2->S1 D2 steps where the trial's D1 reward input was 0. This is a graded effect, as the explanation says, not a separate class.

False positives are a2->S1 D2 steps with prev_reward==1 where the unit stays silent. In the examples these often come after earlier a1 choices or an earlier rare a2->S1. That fits the claim that the unit tracks the agent's confidence in a2. Adding choice<-4.4 removes some of them (test F1 0.826 vs 0.809), a small gain that does not overturn the label.
Tried and rejected as alternatives (test F1): prev_action==2 / stay 0.715; good==2 0.694; prev_common conditions 0.72-0.79. None beats prev_reward==1.

Small caveat: `choice` is the model's logit at the D2 step itself, not at GO. The explanation's 'confidence in a2' should be read that way. The recorded predicate uses only observed inputs, as claimed.
